topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and states its learning objectives.

topics.label: Genetic evolution and the foundations of cancer susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how mutations accumulate and enable cancer development within a susceptible cell and a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risk versus chance and genetic predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how far cancer risk can be attributed to environmental exposures rather than chance or genetic predisposition.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections contribute to carcinogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed example.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage that can become cancer-driving mutations.

topics.label: Tumour promotion and two-stage carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why mutational initiation may require subsequent promotion before tumours develop.

topics.label: Tissue and developmental susceptibility, with a recap of carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: The account of tissue susceptibility completes the mechanistic discussion of carcinogenesis that the following subtopic recaps.

topics.label: Human evidence linking carcinogen exposure to cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how evidence from human samples and populations can connect carcinogen exposure with cancer development.

topics.label: Experimental carcinogenicity testing and its limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess how experimental tests detect carcinogenic potential and why their results may not fully predict human cancer risk.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing distils the lecture's conclusions into the risk–benefit decisions surrounding carcinogen exposure.
